headline: GOLD SURGES 3% TO $4,041 — Democratic Congress Sweep Crushes Dollar; Silver Leaps 4.3% to $51.91
snippet: Democrats secured control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections, sending the US dollar to a one-month low and driving precious metals sharply higher. Spot gold surged 2.85% to $4,041.30 per ounce while silver jumped 4.32% to $51.91 — reversing weeks of selling pressure and returning gold above a key psychological threshold that has capped multiple rally attempts since October. This is the largest single-day gain for precious metals since the Iran war shock in mid-2026.

headline: I-80 GOLD Q3 PRODUCTION EXPLODES 166% — Yet Shares Fall 5% as $140M Capital Hole Spooks Market
snippet: i-80 Gold Corp reported Q3 2026 production 166% above the prior-year quarter as multiple Nevada mines ramped simultaneously under its hub-and-spoke development model. Despite the milestone, shares fell approximately 5% as analysts zeroed in on $140 million in capital requirements over the next 12 months set against a $464 million cash balance — complicated by the Lone Tree processing hub remaining unpermitted for its new design and not expected to commission until late 2027. The divergence between strong production and weak stock illustrates the classic capital-intensity discount applied to mid-tier gold developers.

headline: GOLD CROSSES $4,000: Which 10 Miners Have Best Leverage to the Rally? Goldman Still $4,900
snippet: An Investing.com analysis identifies ten gold mining stocks with the strongest near-term rebound potential following today's $4,000 reclaim, ranked on reserve quality, cost structure and balance-sheet flexibility. Newmont's lowered AISC target of approximately $1,520 per ounce features prominently; Goldman Sachs' year-end $4,900 gold target — implying another 21% upside from current levels — remains the analyst community's highest-conviction call and sets a credible ceiling for a year-end re-rating of the sector.

headline: MIDTERM SWEEP ROUTS DOLLAR AND YIELDS — Precious Metals, Copper Surge as Rate Hike Odds Compress
snippet: The Democratic congressional sweep triggered the sharpest single-day repricing of US rate expectations since the summer rate pause: futures markets cut near-term hike probability by roughly 10 percentage points as a divided Congress is seen reducing the probability of further fiscal tightening. The resulting dollar weakness drove a broad commodity rally extending beyond gold and silver to LME copper, which added to last week's rebound from a 2.5-month low. Analysts note that a sustained easing in dollar strength is historically the most reliable macro precondition for the next leg of a junior mining bull market.

headline: SUNSTONE METALS 126M @ 0.41 G/T AUEQ AT BRAMADEROS — Ecuador Porphyry Extends Before Drill Permits
snippet: Sunstone Metals' final trench result at the Porotillo sector of its Bramaderos porphyry copper-gold project in Ecuador returned 126.32 metres at 0.41 g/t gold-equivalent, extending the mineralised footprint of the target beyond the central pit area. The wide intercept supports the geological model for a large bulk-tonnage porphyry system; the company is now finalising drill permit applications to follow up these surface results with deep diamond holes designed to test the porphyry core at depth.

headline: NORTHERN SHIELD EXTENDS CRESTON COPPER PORPHYRY VIA TRENCHING — Newfoundland TSXV Junior Confirms Broad Mineralisation
snippet: Northern Shield Resources (TSXV: NRN) extended the surface expression of porphyry copper mineralisation at its Creston, Root & Cellar targets in Newfoundland through trench sampling, adding new areas of copper-bearing rock beyond previously mapped extents. The confirmation of continuous copper mineralisation over a larger footprint strengthens the geological case for a future drill program at a time when physical copper demand from China — evidenced by the Yangshan premium near $200/t — remains exceptionally firm.

headline: HEAVY RARE EARTHS CLEARS RADIUM HILL HERITAGE HURDLE — SA Uranium-REE-Scandium Project Nears Drill Phase
snippet: Heavy Rare Earths Ltd (ASX: HRE) received Aboriginal Heritage clearance from South Australia's heritage office for all planned drill areas at the Radium Hill project — a combined uranium, rare earth element and scandium project on the site of Australia's first commercial uranium mine, which operated in the 1950s. With heritage cleared, the remaining hurdle is state regulator approval of EPBC documentation before drilling begins. The timing is notable: clearance arrives just days before China's rare-earth export control suspension expires on November 10.

headline: ENERGY FUELS: URANIUM COMPANY BUILDS US RARE EARTH BUSINESS — White Mesa Now Primary Producer of Heavy REEs for First Time in Decades
snippet: An in-depth Crux Investor analysis profiles how Energy Fuels (NYSE: UUUU) used its White Mesa uranium mill — the last US conventional uranium processing facility — to become the sole American primary producer of critical heavy rare earth oxides including terbium and dysprosium. Construction to expand REE output is underway, targeting Phase 1 production of heavy REE oxides by late 2027. With the Chinese export control suspension expiring November 10 and the Pentagon actively seeking non-Chinese heavy REE supply, Energy Fuels' dual uranium-REE mandate positions it at the intersection of two of the market's most urgent supply-chain concerns.

headline: BMO-EUROZ HARTLEYS DEAL CLOSES — World's Largest Mining Capital Markets Franchise Now Spans Toronto to Sydney
snippet: BMO Capital Markets completed its acquisition of Euroz Hartleys' equities research, institutional sales, ECM and M&A business — Australia's leading junior-mining focused investment bank — creating what the bank calls the world's largest integrated metals and mining capital markets franchise. For junior mining companies seeking institutional coverage and equity capital market access in both the TSX-V and ASX simultaneously, BMO's expanded platform represents a significant new avenue: Canadian juniors with Australian assets, or ASX juniors targeting a TSX-V dual-listing, can now access one of the deepest pools of mining-specialist institutional investors on either side of the Pacific.

headline: STANDARD LITHIUM'S $1.5B SMACKOVER FID IMMINENT — Equinor JV, DOE Grant, Trafigura Offtake All Locked; Year-End Decision Targeted
snippet: Standard Lithium (NYSE: SLI) is targeting a final investment decision on its South West Arkansas lithium project before year-end 2026, with virtually every major precondition now met: Equinor as 45% JV partner, a $225 million US DOE grant, binding offtake agreements with Trafigura and LG Energy Solution covering approximately 89% of planned output, and the last key construction contract awarded. A positive FID would trigger a full notice to proceed and set SWA on course for first commercial lithium carbonate production in 2029 — the first large-scale US domestic lithium facility built with a mix of strategic industrial capital and government co-investment.
